q: Which pair of properties is typical of a simple molecular compound?
options: High melting point and conducts electricity when molten
Low melting point and does not conduct electricity
Low melting point and conducts electricity when solid
High melting point and does not conduct electricity
explain: Simple molecular compounds have weak forces between molecules and no ions or free electrons to carry charge.

q: In a molecule of carbon dioxide, CO₂, how many pairs of electrons are shared in total?
explain: Each carbon–oxygen bond is a double bond (two shared pairs), and there are two of them.

q: Calcium has proton number 20. Which statement about a calcium atom is correct?
options: It has 2 occupied shells and 4 outer electrons, so it is in Period 2, Group IV
It has 4 occupied shells and 8 outer electrons, so it is in Period 4, Group VIII
It has 2 occupied shells and 2 outer electrons, so it is in Period 2, Group II
It has 4 occupied shells and 2 outer electrons, so it is in Period 4, Group II
explain: Calcium is 2,8,8,2: four shells give Period 4 and two outer electrons give Group II.

q: Carbon-14 is an isotope of carbon with proton number 6. How many neutrons does an atom of carbon-14 have?
explain: Neutrons = mass number − proton number = 14 − 6 = 8.

q: Which description of the formation of magnesium oxide is correct?
options: Each magnesium atom shares two electrons with an oxygen atom
Each oxygen atom transfers two electrons to a magnesium atom
Each magnesium atom transfers two electrons to an oxygen atom, forming Mg²⁺ and O²⁻
Each magnesium atom transfers one electron to an oxygen atom
explain: Magnesium (2,8,2) loses two electrons and oxygen (2,6) gains two, so both ions have the configuration 2,8.

q: What is the relative charge of an electron?
explain: An electron has a relative charge of −1. Its relative mass is very small (about 1/1840), which is separate from its charge.

q: Which statement describes a compound?
options: Two or more elements mixed together in any proportions
A substance made of only one type of atom
Two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio
A substance that can be separated by filtration
explain: A compound has atoms of different elements chemically bonded in a fixed ratio; a mixture has no chemical bonding between its parts.

q: What is the formula of the ionic compound formed from Al³⁺ and O²⁻ ions?
options: AlO
Al₂O₃
Al₃O₂
Al₂O
explain: Two Al³⁺ give +6 and three O²⁻ give −6, so the ratio is 2 : 3.

q: Why do isotopes of the same element have the same chemical properties?
options: They have the same number of electrons and the same electronic configuration
They have the same number of neutrons
They have the same mass number
They have the same relative atomic mass
explain: Chemical reactions involve the electrons, and isotopes have identical electron arrangements, so they react in the same way.

q: Compared with a proton, how does the mass of an electron compare?
options: It is much smaller, about 1/1840 of the mass
It is the same
It is about twice as large
It is exactly zero
explain: An electron has a very small mass, about 1/1840 of a proton, so it is negligible when calculating mass number.

q: A sodium atom has 11 protons. How many electrons does the Na⁺ ion contain?
explain: The ion has lost one electron from the neutral atom, so 11 − 1 = 10.

q: Why are the Group VIII noble gases very unreactive?
options: Their atoms have only one outer electron
Their atoms have a full outer shell of electrons
Their atoms have no electrons
Their atoms have empty outer shells
explain: A full outer shell is a stable arrangement, so noble gas atoms do not need to gain, lose or share electrons.

q: In lithium fluoride, how many electrons are in the outer shell of the fluoride ion, F⁻?
explain: The fluorine atom (2,7) gains one electron from lithium, giving 2,8 with 8 outer electrons.

q: Copper has two isotopes: ⁶³Cu (69%) and ⁶⁵Cu (31%). What is the relative atomic mass of copper, to one decimal place?
Why does a hammered ionic crystal shatter while a hammered metal bends?
options: Metals have weaker bonds than ionic compounds
In an ionic crystal like ions are forced next to each other and repel, but in a metal the electrons keep the ions bonded
Ionic crystals have no bonds between ions
Metals have fewer particles than ionic crystals
explain: Moving layers in an ionic lattice line up like charges, which repel and split the crystal; in metals the sea of electrons maintains bonding.

q: Which row correctly classifies each substance?
options: compound | element | mixture
element | mixture | compound
element | compound | mixture
mixture | compound | element
explain: Sodium contains one type of atom (element), carbon dioxide has carbon and oxygen chemically bonded (compound) and seawater is salt dissolved in water (mixture).

q: How many other carbon atoms is each carbon atom bonded to in diamond?
explain: In diamond each carbon atom forms four strong covalent bonds in a tetrahedral arrangement.

q: Which statement defines isotopes?
options: Atoms of different elements with the same number of neutrons
Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of protons
Atoms with the same mass number but different proton numbers
explain: Isotopes have the same proton number, so they are the same element, but different neutron numbers give different mass numbers.

q: Which row correctly describes a metal?
options: positive ions and negative ions | conducts when solid
positive ions and delocalised electrons | conducts when solid
positive ions and delocalised electrons | does not conduct when solid
neutral molecules | conducts when solid
explain: A metal lattice contains positive ions and delocalised electrons, which allow it to conduct even as a solid.

q: Iron filings and sulfur powder are stirred together, giving a mixture. The mixture is then heated strongly and iron(II) sulfide forms. Which statement is correct?
options: Iron(II) sulfide is a mixture, because it contains iron and sulfur
Iron(II) sulfide is a compound, and iron can be removed from the mixture with a magnet but not from the compound
Iron(II) sulfide is an element, because it is a single solid
Iron can be removed from iron(II) sulfide with a magnet, as in the mixture
explain: In the compound the iron is chemically bonded to sulfur, so it loses its magnetic behaviour; in the mixture the iron keeps its properties and can be pulled out by a magnet.

q: Bronze is made by melting copper and tin together. Which statement about bronze is correct?
options: It is a mixture, because the copper and tin are not chemically combined in a fixed ratio
It is a compound, because it is made by heating
It is an element, because it looks like a single metal
It is a compound, because it has a higher melting point than tin
explain: Bronze (an alloy) is a mixture of metals; its composition can vary and the metals are not chemically bonded to form a compound.

q: Which method can be used to break a compound down into its elements?
options: Filtering it
Using a magnet
Passing an electric current through it when molten (electrolysis)
Letting it evaporate
explain: The elements in a compound are chemically bonded, so a chemical change such as electrolysis is needed; physical methods separate only mixtures.

q: In a sodium chloride lattice, how is each ion surrounded?
options: By ions of the same charge
By neutral molecules
By delocalised electrons
By ions of the opposite charge
explain: The lattice alternates positive and negative ions so that attractions between opposite charges are maximised.

q: Which of these is a mixture?
options: Air
Carbon dioxide
Sodium chloride
Pure water
explain: Air contains nitrogen, oxygen and other gases that are not chemically joined, so it is a mixture. The others are pure compounds.

q: Which pair of elements forms a covalent compound?
options: Sodium and chlorine
Magnesium and oxygen
Potassium and fluorine
Carbon and chlorine
explain: Covalent bonds form between non-metal atoms. The other pairs each contain a metal and a non-metal.

q: What is the electronic configuration of a sodium ion, Na⁺ (sodium has proton number 11)?
explain: The sodium atom (2,8,1) loses one electron to form Na⁺, leaving 10 electrons arranged 2,8.

q: Why is graphite used for the electrodes in electrolysis?
options: It conducts electricity because it contains ions
It is very hard
It conducts electricity because it has delocalised electrons
It has a low melting point
explain: Each carbon atom in graphite uses only three outer electrons for bonding, leaving one delocalised electron that carries charge.

q: Why is silicon(IV) oxide hard and has a high melting point?
options: It has strong forces between separate molecules
It has a lattice of positive ions in a sea of electrons
It has layers that slide over each other
It has a giant structure of strong covalent bonds, like diamond
explain: Its giant covalent lattice means a very large number of strong bonds have to be broken to melt it.

q: In a molecule of ethene, C₂H₄, how many pairs of electrons are shared in total?
explain: There are four C–H single bonds (4 pairs) and a C=C double bond (2 pairs), giving 6 shared pairs.

q: What is the nature of the force that holds a metallic lattice together?
options: Attraction between shared pairs of electrons and nuclei only
Repulsion between neighbouring positive ions
Attraction between positive ions and negative delocalised electrons
Attraction between metal ions and non-metal ions
explain: Oppositely charged ions and electrons attract each other electrostatically; this is stronger than the repulsion between ions.
